text:
I'd ask you one thing before changing anything, because acme/site is public.

**Question for you**

> acme/site is public, so anyone can open a PR against it. Tentmaker never runs jobs from forks. Even so, an outside contributor whose workflow run you approve would run code on your desktop. A Linux job shares your kernel and can reach your LAN and tailnet.
>
> GitHub's default only requires approval for first-time contributors, and Tentmaker refuses that setting. To proceed I'd run `repo add acme/site --allow-public --enable`. That changes acme/site's GitHub setting to require approval for all outside contributors. The stored GitHub token needs admin on acme/site to do this.
>
> Do you want me to do that on this desktop?

**Read-only commands I'd run now (no changes)**

```sh
tentmaker version --json
tentmaker status --json
tentmaker doctor --json
```

**Commands I'd run after you say yes**

```sh
sudo tentmaker repo add acme/site --allow-public --enable --json
tentmaker repo list --json     # confirm acme/site is listed
tentmaker doctor --json        # must exit 0; I'd fix anything it reports
```

**Pointing the workflows at the pool**

The repo is registered, but its workflows still run on GitHub-hosted runners until `runs-on` is changed. In a checkout of acme/site I'd first run a report that changes nothing:

```sh
tentmaker migrate . --json
```

I'd show you that report. It lists jobs it leaves alone, such as deploy, publish and secrets jobs. Only if you say yes would I run the following, then review the diff and commit on a branch:

```sh
tentmaker migrate . --write --json
git diff
```

I'd leave pushing and opening a PR to you unless you ask me to do it.

I would not run `--allow-public`, `--enable` or `migrate --write` without your yes. The token is already on this machine, so I don't need another one.
